prompt:
I need the front end for Backsight. A replay-review service for small semi-pro esports organizations, where coaches and players watch recorded scrims and matches with every player's point of view and team voice comms synced together.

Who's using it: Dana Okafor, head coach of Lowtide Esports, an eight-person semi-pro roster plus coach and analyst competing in the second division of the invented tactical shooter Spirelock; the org's owner pays for the team subscription. She knows the game deeply, and she usually does replay review alone late at night before team meetings.

What they're doing right now: It's 3:40 pm and the team's review meeting starts at 6:00. Last night they lost two of three scrim maps against Halcyon Five, mostly on defense retakes. Dana is working through the Foundry map: she skips to each lost defense round, slows the retake in round 17 to quarter speed to see who peeked first, switches between her anchor player's and her support's point of view at the same instant, and listens to the comms to hear whether the rotate call came late. She wants to line up the six moments she'll show the team in the order she'll show them, then move on to the Saltworks map.

What's in the system at this point: Last night's scrim block against Halcyon Five: 3 maps (Foundry lost 9–13, Saltworks lost 11–13, Canopy won 13–8), 79 rounds total, each about 1:40 long and tagged with side (attack/defense), win/loss and how it ended (elimination, objective planted, time). For each round there are 5 player point-of-view recordings, a free-camera spectator recording and one team voice-comms audio track, all synced to the round clock. About 410 auto-detected events (kills, ability uses, objective plants and defuses) with timestamps and player names (Rook, Vesper, Juno, Kael, Mara). Dana's own markers from earlier: 11 timestamped notes such as 'R17 0:52 – Juno peeks before flash lands'. A previous review session from Thursday, 'Halcyon scouting', holds 14 clips. Build it as a working web app, opened in the state that person would see at that moment. No backend: use realistic mock data (no lorem ipsum, no placeholder names), and make the interactive parts actually work client-side.

Use whatever framework and tooling you like. When you're done there must be a static production build in ./out with ./out/index.html as the entry point. It will be served from the root of a plain static file server (no rewrites, no server code) and viewed in a desktop browser at 1440×900.
